references.title: Human articular chondrocytes express functional leukotriene B4 receptors.
references.note: human articular chondrocytes, healthy and OA: both LTB4 receptors present, LTB4 signals through BLT1 (ERK1/2)

references.title: Inhibition of Leukotriene A(4) Hydrolase Suppressed Cartilage Degradation and Synovial Inflammation in a Mouse Model of Experimental Osteoarthritis.
references.note: human OA cartilage and mouse experimental OA: BLT1 and LTA4H high in OA, LTA4H inhibition suppresses cartilage damage and synovitis

references.title: Structural basis of leukotriene B4 receptor 1 activation.
references.note: cryo-EM of human BLT1 bound to LTB4 (with Gi), the binding site resolved

references.title: A G-protein-coupled receptor for leukotriene B4 that mediates chemotaxis.
references.note: cloned human BLT1: specific LTB4 binding, Kd 0.154 nM, calcium and InsP3 rise

references.title: A second leukotriene B(4) receptor, BLT2. A new therapeutic target in inflammation and immunological disorders.
references.note: cloned human BLT2: LTB4 Kd 23 nM against 1.1 nM for BLT1, a second, pharmacologically distinct receptor

references.title: Human articular chondrocytes express functional leukotriene B4 receptors.
references.note: human OA and healthy chondrocytes: LTB4 signalling through BLT1 to ERK1/2, blocked by a BLT1 antagonist

references.title: Leukotriene B4 activates intracellular calcium and augments human osteoclastogenesis.
references.note: human osteoclast precursors (inflammatory arthritis, not OA): LTB4 through BLT1 and BLT2 activates phospholipase C and calcium flux, so the receptors do run a Gq-type pathway in human joint cells

references.title: Signalling through the leukotriene B4 receptor involves both alphai and alpha16, but not alphaq or alpha11 G-protein subunits.
references.note: human BLT1 in COS-7: inositol phosphates need Galpha16, not Gq or G11; the Gq-family partner is G16 (GNA15)

references.title: Structural basis of leukotriene B4 receptor 1 activation.
references.note: human BLT1 in complex with a heterotrimeric G protein (Gi), showing the receptor-G protein complex of this receptor

references.title: Reconstitution of agonist-stimulated phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate hydrolysis using purified m1 muscarinic receptor, Gq/11, and phospholipase C-beta 1.
references.note: purified receptor and Gq/11 reconstituted: the agonist-bound receptor engages and activates Gq/11 with no other protein needed

references.title: Human articular chondrocytes express functional leukotriene B4 receptors.
references.note: human OA chondrocytes: LTB4 through BLT1 drives downstream signalling, the receptor's G protein cycle by extension

references.title: Reconstitution of agonist-stimulated phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate hydrolysis using purified m1 muscarinic receptor, Gq/11, and phospholipase C-beta 1.
references.note: purified receptor with Gq/11: agonist raises GTPgammaS binding 20 to 50-fold, the receptor catalysing nucleotide exchange on Gqalpha and Galpha11

references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.title: Structural basis for the specific inhibition of heterotrimeric Gq protein by a small molecule.
references.note: crystal structure of human Gqalpha-beta-gamma with YM-254890: the inhibitor blocks exchange by holding GDP, which identifies GDP release as the step

references.title: G proteins: transducers of receptor-generated signals.
references.note: review of the G protein cycle: the receptor catalyses GDP for GTP exchange on the alpha subunit

references.title: G proteins: transducers of receptor-generated signals.
references.note: no abstract; classic review of the G protein cycle (receptor-catalysed GDP-GTP exchange, alpha-GTP and beta-gamma separating, hydrolysis, reassociation); no human data

references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.title: Neuronal prostaglandin E2 receptor subtype EP3 mediates antinociception during inflammation.
references.note: NOT an OA model: rat inflamed joint (inflammation model, not named in the abstract; full text not open) shows EP3 on DRG and spinal neurons antinociceptive via Gi; the OA part is human: EP3 in joint nerves of patients with painful OA (covers the pathway's steps by extension)

references.title: Shear-induced interleukin-6 synthesis in chondrocytes: roles of E prostanoid (EP) 2 and EP3 in cAMP/protein kinase A- and PI3-K/Akt-dependent NF-kappaB activation.
references.note: human T/C-28a2 chondrocytes under high shear (an in vitro OA-like model, cartilage not neurons): EP3 down-regulation raises cAMP, ectopic EP3 blocks the PKA pathway

references.title: Inhibition of adenylyl cyclase by Gi alpha.
references.note: purified activated Gi alpha inhibits adenylyl cyclases directly (myristoylation needed; recombinant)

references.title: Cloning and expression of a prostaglandin E receptor EP3 subtype from human erythroleukaemia cells.
references.note: human EP3 in COS-1 cells: PGE2 inhibits forskolin-stimulated cAMP formation (receptor level, Gi not shown directly)

props: Receptor for prostaglandin E2 (PGE2). The activity of this receptor is mediated by G(q) proteins which activate a phosphatidylinositol-calcium second messenger system.
PLC-154; Phosphoinositide phospholipase C-beta-1; Phospholipase C-I; Phospholipase C-beta-1

Catalyzes the hydrolysis of 1-phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate into diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) and mediates intracellular signaling downstream of G protein-coupled receptors. Regulates the function of the endothelial barrier

The production of the second messenger molecules diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) is mediated by activated phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C enzymes. In neutrophils, participates in a phospholipase C-activating N-formyl peptide-activated GPCR (G protein-coupled receptor) signaling pathway by promoting RASGRP4 activation by DAG, to promote neutrophil functional responses

Catalyzes the production of the second messenger molecules diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3). Key transducer of G protein-coupled receptor signaling: activated by G(q)/G(11) G alpha proteins downstream of G protein-coupled receptors activation.

Activated phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C enzymes catalyze the production of the second messenger molecules diacylglycerol (DAG) and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) involved in G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathways. PLCB4 is a direct effector of the endothelin receptor signaling pathway that plays an essential role in lower jaw and middle ear structures development

references.title: Adrenergic signalling in osteoarthritis.
references.note: both cells (by extension): review of adrenergic signalling in OA, the receptors and their signalling pathways; no Gi coupling in joint neurons shown

references.title: Protein kinase A-mediated phosphorylation of the beta 2-adrenergic receptor regulates its coupling to Gs and Gi. Demonstration in a reconstituted system.
references.note: both cells: purified recombinant beta2AR with purified heterotrimeric Gs and Gi; PKA phosphorylation of the receptor raises Gi coupling measured as receptor-stimulated GTPgammaS binding - the cleanest biochemical evidence for the step, in no neuron

references.title: Switching of the coupling of the beta2-adrenergic receptor to different G proteins by protein kinase A.
references.note: both cells: human HEK293 cells; beta2AR signals through pertussis-toxin-sensitive G protein betagamma and needs PKA sites - the key step paper, but Gi coupling is inferred from pertussis toxin and ERK, not measured directly, and it is contradicted by Friedman 2002 (see weak_points)

references.title: Stress induces a switch of intracellular signaling in sensory neurons in a model of generalized pain.
references.note: nociceptor: rat sensory afferents after sound stress; adrenaline receptor coupling switches from Gs to Gi, giving prolonged hyperalgesia (the block's own rationale; a generalized pain model, not OA)

references.title: Agonist dose-dependent phosphorylation by protein kinase A and G protein-coupled receptor kinase regulates beta2 adrenoceptor coupling to G(i) proteins in cardiomyocytes.
references.note: both cells: mouse cardiac myocytes; beta2AR-Gi coupling needs the PKA sites and only occurs at high agonist concentrations (and also needs GRK phosphorylation)

references.title: Adrenergic signalling in osteoarthritis.
references.note: both cells (by extension): review of adrenergic signalling in OA, receptors and their signalling pathways

references.title: Protein kinase A-mediated phosphorylation of the beta 2-adrenergic receptor regulates its coupling to Gs and Gi. Demonstration in a reconstituted system.
references.note: both cells: the PKA-phosphorylated beta2AR catalyses GTPgammaS binding to purified Gi - receptor-catalysed nucleotide exchange for this very receptor pair

references.title: Structures of active conformations of Gi alpha 1 and the mechanism of GTP hydrolysis.
references.note: both cells: GTPgammaS-Gi alpha1 structure; the disordered N-terminus suggests how betagamma is released (rat recombinant)

references.title: G proteins: transducers of receptor-generated signals.
references.note: both cells: classic G protein review (no abstract on PubMed): GTP-bound alpha and betagamma separate from the receptor

references.title: Adrenergic signalling in osteoarthritis.
references.note: both cells (by extension): review of adrenergic signalling in OA, receptors and their signalling pathways

references.title: Structures of active conformations of Gi alpha 1 and the mechanism of GTP hydrolysis.
references.note: both cells: Gi alpha1 GTPgammaS and GDP.AlF4 structures; Gln204 and Arg178 in the intrinsic hydrolysis (rat recombinant)

references.title: GAIP and RGS4 are GTPase-activating proteins for the Gi subfamily of G protein alpha subunits.
references.note: both cells: GAIP (human) and RGS4 accelerate GTP hydrolysis by Gi-family alpha at least 40-fold (purified proteins) - the RGS modifier

references.title: Structure of RGS4 bound to AlF4--activated G(i alpha1): stabilization of the transition state for GTP hydrolysis.
references.note: both cells: RGS4 bound to AlF4-activated Gi alpha1; RGS stabilises the switch regions in the transition state (rat recombinant)

references.title: Adrenergic signalling in osteoarthritis.
references.note: both cells (by extension): review of adrenergic signalling in OA, receptors and their signalling pathways

references.title: The structure of the G protein heterotrimer Gi alpha 1 beta 1 gamma 2.
references.note: both cells: structure of the Gi alpha1(GDP) beta1 gamma2 heterotrimer; betagamma stabilises the inactive GDP-bound alpha (recombinant, non-human)

references.title: G proteins: transducers of receptor-generated signals.
references.note: both cells: classic G protein review (no abstract on PubMed): GDP-bound alpha reassociates with betagamma

references.title: Adrenergic signalling in osteoarthritis.
references.note: both cells (by extension): review of adrenergic signalling in OA, receptors and their signalling pathways including the cAMP arm

references.title: Inhibition of adenylyl cyclase by Gi alpha.
references.note: both cells: purified activated Gi alpha inhibits adenylyl cyclases directly, myristoylation required (recombinant)

references.title: Coupling of beta2-adrenoceptor to Gi proteins and its physiological relevance in murine cardiac myocytes.
references.note: both cells: mouse cardiac myocytes (with human beta2AR in the transgenics); beta2AR stimulation labels Gi2 and Gi3 alpha, and pertussis toxin restores the cAMP response - beta2-driven Gi opposing the cyclase in a cell

references.title: Stress induces a switch of intracellular signaling in sensory neurons in a model of generalized pain.
references.note: nociceptor: rat; after stress the switch to Gi changes the cAMP-dependent response of sensory neurons to adrenaline (effect on the cyclase arm in the drawn cell type)

Catalyzes the formation of cAMP in response to calcium entry leadings to cAMP signaling activation that affect processes suche as synaptic plasticity and insulin secretion. nodes.label: ADRA2A
props: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor subtype C10; Alpha-2A adrenoreceptor

Alpha-2 adrenergic receptors are G protein-coupled receptors for catecholamines that activate the G(i/o) protein pathway, thereby promoting adenylyl cyclase inhibition, ERK1/2 stimulation, and voltage-gated calcium channels suppression.
